reason: r20 is r19's enter-hook clip box plus the row lifecycle. MHGU quests are divided into areas with a loading screen between them (the tester's account of 2026-10-24, matching every run's log: HUD-absent stretches, r18's bar rect moving from 110,38,238,166 to 220,70,348,198 at t=236, then freed objects from t=873), so the gauge row, and with it the inserted mask, the 5-word object array and the 9-record draw block, belongs to one area. When the mask's parent link stops pointing at the captured root, r20 clears the sampler's controller, the instance capture, the row facts state and the insertion's addresses: the same re-arm the root destructor hook performs, on the signal the r18 run proved necessary (that hook has fired zero times in six sessions, and r18 wrote into a freed mask for 90 s). The insertion itself is r18's, and r18 proved it lands: mask 0x48003060, a 5-word array through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator with instance+0xd8 and root+0xa0 published, a draw block resized through the root's vtable slot 0x58 with main+0xa49b28's arithmetic from the row+8 pair (3 objects, 16 sequences: 56 bytes = 7 records, grown to 72 = 9). What r18 did not prove is the clip: 376 of 383 probe lines read left == right, the scissor zero-width, because the rectangle at mask+0xb0..+0xbc is the game's layout's derived value and a node the animation row has no entry for has quad width 0. r19 moved the write into the mask's enter handler (main+0xa4ba94), in the call that applies it, and r20 keeps that. Not approved for distribution; r12 and r13 were packaged and never run.
runtime_test: NOT RUN: r20 re-arms the whole gauge row path when the inserted mask's links are lost, so a hunt that crosses quest areas gets a mask in each area's row. r19 (the enter-hook write site) was never run. r18 ran once on Eden 2026-10-24 (installed bytes 55340cfbec4fbdc176be57d3ac22356945c4f431f882eb784b362426a1e23330): the insertion completed and the user reported the gauge missing, with 376 of 383 probe lines at a zero-width box and ~90 s of writes into a freed mask. r17/r16/r15 ran clean; r14 ran once and failed as reported.

limitations: r4 has no runtime test; its lines, the 320-sample budget and the absence of any drawing change are static results.
r2 was built and never run; r3 was run once on Eden and is recorded.
r14 was run once on Eden and failed as reported: the gauge was clipped away from the insertion and the game crashed at the quest end. Its log is the evidence, and the insertion is removed in r15.

r15 was run once on Eden and drew the gauge normally for 740 seconds with no exception; its facts line printed tree_nodes 3 against 4 objects, and its object-list fields were read from the wrong object (the controller's owner field), which is what r16 fixes.

r16 changes nothing on screen: it reads game memory and logs. No drawing, no gauge change, and no cleanup claim (the root-destructor hook fired zero times in the three sessions that logged it). Its Eden run ended in Eden's own shutdown records (maxwell_3d Critical asserts, ForceStop, host SIGSEGV) with zero guest exceptions.
the game's destructor is assumed to free the map block r17 publishes through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator; that free has not been observed, and r17 frees the old 4-word block itself
The per-weapon tier tables live in RomFS weapon data and are not read in this workspace: no weapon data file is extracted here.
The gauge itself is not part of r4.

r20 has not been run, and neither has r19's enter-hook write site: the one completed insertion (r18) hid the gauge with a zero-width box, and the re-arm that lets a hunt crossing quest areas get a mask per row has no runtime evidence
